Bounded independent reproduction: apply single-site depolarization directly to dense matrices, integrate in s=u^α using 256-point Gauss–Legendre quadrature on [0,1], and transpose only the first tensor factor. For n=3,4,5 and α=0.25,0.8,1.6 the maximum entry discrepancy in the primary compression was 1.61×10^(−10). Separately, scalar quadratures of the primary block through n=120 at c=0.3 and 0.8 showed trends toward the predicted limits.
correctness.rationale: For r1<r2 the older exponential age has the law of the younger age plus an independent mixture of zero and an exponential of rate r1; the mixture of additional local channels preserves PPT. The strictly PPT mixed-state limit and the NPT pure-W limit, together with continuity, give one positive finite boundary with PPT at equality. For the primary compression, applying the single-site channel gives p q^m on the vacuum, and on the first-qubit-one symmetric singleton it gives p q^(m−2)[2q²+(m−1)(p²+u²)]/n. Both equal 2^(−n) at u=0 and their beta-average corrections are o(2^(−n)): on u≤1/2 their derivatives are bounded by a polynomial times (3/4)^n, and on u≥1/2 the p factor makes their integrals O(n^(−2)). The primary coherence has two factors of u and an endpoint integral asymptotic to 2/n, so its scaled magnitude tends to 2c. The other off-diagonal blocks are subset-incidence matrices between k and k+1. They have constant row and column sums, hence the stated norm, with ratio to the primary block bounded by O(√n) times the k=1 integral ratio O(1/n). After pinching the first-qubit diagonal blocks, the low-u segment u≤n^(−2) alone supplies the lower bound (1−o(1))2^(−n)I by the Pauli expansion and beta mass n^(−2α_n); contributions at higher u are positive semidefinite in the pinching. This yields the matching full-matrix lower bound to the primary-block Rayleigh upper bound. The finite-size interval property and sign tests for fixed c on both sides of 1/2 then give the claimed threshold limit.
residual_risks: The dense replay checks block entries only at the tested rates; the larger-size numerics check only the primary block. Neither substitutes for the uniform complement and pinching bounds. No claim is made about the sign at exactly c=1/2, PPT implying separability, or genuine multipartite entanglement.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the all-size one-cut threshold and, especially, the quantitative crossover 2^n λ_min→1−2c at r/γ=c n^(3/2)2^(−n) for the common-age mixture of locally depolarized W states. value.rationale: The threshold and crossover quantify a naturally posed stationary entanglement transition: the critical rate is exponentially small with a precise n^(3/2)/2 prefactor multiplying γ2^(−n), and the scaled eigenvalue describes behavior on both sides. The result is informative precisely because the oldest, nearly mixed part of the ensemble and the rare young coherent part contribute on the same scale here.
residual_risks: The negative eigenvalue is itself exponentially small in the crossover window; this is not evidence of robustness to fixed experimental errors, nor does the model account for the cost of global repreparation.
